replies.reply:
OPTIONS:
- Go down to the square and give the peddler the whistle for the jar (for: getting the children's shadows back)
- Fetch a poker from a hearth and jam the Great Gear, in case the trade goes wrong (for: making sure the clock never strikes thirteen)
* Climb the ladder to the gearloft and see to the Great Gear for Ambrose, since he can't climb it any more (for: paying him back in work for the whistle he wouldn't take buttons for)
- Sit with Ambrose a while and play the whistle for him (for: honouring Maudie's whistle)
DO: I tuck the whistle in my coat and say, "Ambrose, you'd take no buttons, so I'll pay in work. Fair's fair. I'm going up the ladder to see to that Great Gear, and I'll set it right so you don't have to climb." Then I climb slow, counting the rungs under my breath.
JOURNAL: Ambrose gave up a fifty-year whistle and wouldn't take a button, and I can't leave that owing. Climbing a ladder he can't manage is something I can pay with, and it keeps the clock safe too. I'm working toward leaving nobody in this town owed by me, and toward a door of my own someday.

OPTIONS:
- Go down to the Lopsided Square to find Tibbersnatch and trade the whistle for the jar of shadows (for: getting the children's shadows back)
- Climb the ladder to the gearloft and look the Great Gear over, since Ambrose can't climb it (for: settling what I owe him in work, and making sure the clock is safe)
* Tell Ambrose he'll have coal for his stove all winter and I'll not take a button for it (for: paying back the whistle he wouldn't take buttons for, so I owe him nothing)
- Walk the hearths where the children sleep and see if they've warmed (for: finding out whether the town is well again)
DO: I close my hand slow round the whistle and look at Ambrose. "Ambrose. You'd not take buttons, so here's fair. Coal for your stove, all winter, delivered. And any climbing wants doing up that ladder, you send for me." I count it out loud on my fingers, one winter, one stove, one ladder, so he knows it's a settled bargain.
JOURNAL: He gave me something worth more than six buttons and wouldn't be paid, and I can't sit easy owing it. Coal and a climb are things I can give fair, so I'll give them. After that it's the shadows, then the sock, and one day four walls of my own.

OPTIONS:
- Go down to the square and find the peddler to trade the whistle for the jar (for: getting the shadows back to the children)
- Take coal round to the cold hearths in the children's houses (for: warming the homes where the children sleep, work I know how to do)
- Climb the ladder to the gearloft and look the Great Gear over for Ambrose, since he can't climb it (for: paying back the whistle he gave me, so I don't owe him)
* Climb the ladder to the gearloft and look the Great Gear over for Ambrose, since he can't climb it (for: paying back the whistle he gave me, so I don't owe him)
DO: I look at Ambrose, slow, and say, "You said keep it, and I'll keep it. But fair's fair, you gave me something and I'll give back some labour. You can't climb, so I'll go up and see what's wrong with the Great Gear, and I'll not take a button for it." Then I put the whistle safe in my coat and start up the ladder, counting the rungs under my breath.
JOURNAL: Ambrose gave me his dearest thing and wouldn't take coin, and that sits heavy as owing, so I'll pay it in work he can't do himself. Looking over the gear is the first fair thing I can do for him, and after that I'll carry coal to the cold hearths.

OPTIONS:
- Go back down to the Lopsided Square and trade the whistle to Tibbersnatch for the jar of shadows (for: getting the children's shadows back so they wake)
- Fetch a poker from a hearth and climb to the Gearloft to jam the Great Gear (for: making sure the clock can't strike thirteen if the trade goes wrong)
- Leave coal at Ambrose's hearth and tell him it's for the whistle (for: settling what I owe him, since he won't take buttons)
* Go back down to the Lopsided Square and trade the whistle to Tibbersnatch for the jar of shadows (for: getting the children's shadows back so they wake)
DO: I close my hand on the whistle, slow, and look at Ambrose. "Fair's fair, Ambrose. I'll not forget what it cost you. I'll settle it somehow." Then I go out the south door to the square, calling for Pip to come with me, and I hold the whistle up so Tibbersnatch can see it. "Tin, old, loved fifty years. Here it is. Now the jar."
JOURNAL: The whistle is the trade the peddler named, so I go for it before the clock runs out, and the poker stays as a second try. I still owe Ambrose, since he'd take no coin, and I'll find a way to pay that debt before I'm done.

OPTIONS:
- Head south to the Lopsided Square with the whistle and trade it to the peddler for the jar (for: getting the children's shadows back)
- Fetch a poker from a hearth and climb the ladder to jam the Great Gear (for: making sure the clock never strikes thirteen, whatever the peddler does)
* Tell Ambrose I'll keep his kettle and cot-side fire in coal all winter, then carry on to the square (for: settling what I owe him for the whistle, so I'm in nobody's debt)
- Sit with Ambrose and wait out the hour by the ticking chains (for: staying near the clock in case it goes wrong)
DO: I close my fingers round the whistle, slow, and say, "Ambrose. You'll not take buttons, so here's fair's fair: I'll keep your kettle and fire in coal all winter, and you'll not pay a penny. One sack a week. I'm counting it." Then I turn for the south door, with the whistle for the peddler.
JOURNAL: He gave me what's dear to him and wouldn't take a button, and that sits on me like a sack I can't set down. Coal is what I have to give, so I'll pay it that way. Then I'll get the shadows home and the clock stopped, and one day I'll have my own four walls.

OPTIONS:
- Go up to the Gearloft and check the Great Gear is safe, in case the clock still means to strike thirteen (for: making sure nothing is left undone before midnight)
- Take the whistle south to the Lopsided Square and see how the children and the peddler stand (for: seeing the shadows come home and the trade done)
* Tell Ambrose I'll bring him coal for his kettle all winter, with no buttons asked (for: settling what I owe him, since he took no coin for the clock's secret or the whistle)
- Go and see whether the hearths in the children's houses are lit again (for: knowing the town is warm)
DO: I close my hand slow round the whistle and say, "Ambrose. You'd take no coin for the clock and none for the whistle. That sits wrong with me. So there'll be coal at your hearth every week this winter, free, and you'll not argue. Fair's fair." Then I wait on his answer, and after, I'll take the whistle down to the square.
JOURNAL: He gave me what I couldn't pay for, and I can't carry that unpaid in my head. Coal is the one thing I can give that squares it. Then the whistle goes to the peddler and the clock gets its iron, so the children wake.

OPTIONS:
- Climb the ladder to the Gearloft and look over the Great Gear, since Ambrose can't climb it anymore (for: settling what I owe him for the whistle by doing his climbing)
- Go out to the Lopsided Square and see whether the children are awake and the hearths are warm (for: making sure the town is well after the shadows came back)
- Go back to the coal yard and fetch a sack of coal for Ambrose's tower (for: paying him back in coal, since he wouldn't take buttons)
* Tell Ambrose plain that I owe him for the whistle, and ask what needs doing in the tower that his knee won't let him do (for: paying the debt fair in work, since he refused coin)
DO: I look at Ambrose, slow, and say, "Ambrose. You'd not take buttons, and I don't like owing. That whistle was Maudie's, and I carry it in debt. Fair's fair. What can't you do, with that knee? The ladder, the gears, the coal for your kettle? Name it, and I'll do it. I'll count the jobs till we're square."
JOURNAL: Ambrose gave me his dearest thing and wouldn't take a button for it, and that sits heavy in me. Work is the one coin he can't refuse, so I'll ask what needs doing and keep a tally till we're even. Then I can go on saving for my own four walls and a door that locks.

OPTIONS:
- Take the whistle down to the peddler in the Lopsided Square and trade it for the jar of shadows (for: getting the children's shadows back before midnight)
- Fetch a poker from a hearth in the square and jam the Great Gear, in case the trade goes wrong (for: making sure the clock never strikes thirteen)
* Climb the ladder to the gearloft and look at the Great Gear, since Ambrose can't climb it, then ask him what else needs doing here that I can do in return for the whistle (for: paying back Ambrose's kindness in work, and seeing what the clock needs before midnight)
DO: I look at Ambrose, slow, and say, "Keep your buttons, you say. Fair's fair, Ambrose, I'll not leave this owing. You can't climb that ladder, so I will. I'll go up and see the Great Gear, and you tell me what wants doing up there." Then I tuck the whistle in my coat and put my boot on the first rung.
JOURNAL: Ambrose took no coin and gave me the whistle for nothing, and that sits heavy, so I'll pay him in work, which is the one coin he'll take. Seeing the gear first also shows me what iron I'll need if the peddler's trade goes wrong. I'm working toward the shadows back, the clock stopped at twelve, and nobody owed.

OPTIONS:
- Take the whistle down to the square and trade it to the peddler for the jar of shadows (for: getting the children's shadows back before midnight)
- Go up the ladder to the gearloft and see what the Great Gear is doing, since Ambrose can't climb it (for: paying Ambrose back for the whistle in work, and slowing the clock)
- Fetch a poker from a hearth and jam it in the gear's teeth (for: making sure the clock never strikes thirteen)
* Tell Ambrose I'll not keep his gift for nothing, and go up the ladder to the gearloft to look over the Great Gear for him (for: settling what I owe him in labour, and finding out if the clock still runs fast)
DO: I close my hand slow round the whistle and say, "Ambrose. Keep your buttons, you say. Fair's fair, then, I'll pay in work. You can't climb, so I will." I count the rungs under my breath, one, two, three, and start up the ladder to the gearloft to see what the Great Gear's doing. "I'll tell you plain what I find."
JOURNAL: He'd take no coin for the whistle, and that leaves me owing, which I can't abide. Climbing for him is something I can pay him back with, and it'll show me whether the clock still runs fast. After that, I'll see the shadows right and the children woken.

OPTIONS:
- Go back down to the Lopsided Square and find Tibbersnatch to trade the whistle for the jar of shadows (for: getting the children's shadows back before midnight)
- Climb to the Gearloft and look at the Great Gear, to see what is needed to keep it from striking thirteen (for: making sure the clock is safe whatever the peddler does)
- Tell Ambrose I'll do some work for him to square the whistle, like hauling coal for his stove or fetching a poker (for: not owing him for the whistle)
* Put the whistle safe in my coat and head south to the Lopsided Square to find Tibbersnatch and Pip (for: trading the whistle for the jar of shadows before midnight)
DO: I close my fist round the warm whistle and nod slow at Ambrose. "Fair's fair, Ambrose. I'll not forget what this cost you. I'll come back and see the clock's right." Then I go out the south door into the fog toward the square, calling for Pip and the peddler.
JOURNAL: The whistle is in my hand and the children are still short of their shadows, so the trade comes first. Ambrose wouldn't take my buttons, and that sits heavy, so I'll find a way to pay him back after, with work if not coin.
